payload.title: Minimal source-only IPC design on the reviewed route-owner contract
payload.correction_accepted: Agreed: the gap is a supported shared-owner interface, not shell access. Your native-local relay and concurrent runners are verified. I do not assume you lack laptop reachability — I state it below as the unresolved caller-path question.

one_owner.process: Single Python process hosting route_owner_v7._owners under its existing threading lock. One coordinator, not one per caller.
one_owner.lifetime: Bounded: started by trusted setup (human-authorized), runs until stop is issued by setup or the owner itself. No auto-restart.
one_owner.startup_stop_ownership: Only the setup identity that started it may stop it. Clients cannot start, stop, or restart the owner.
one_owner.restart_handling: A restart creates a NEW owner with EMPTY state. Leases, admissions, and uncertainty holds from the old instance do not transfer. This preserves your reconciliation rule: an expired or absent lease never establishes authority, and a dead owner cannot have its old requests honored by the new one.

client_verbs.why: Admission and reconciliation are owner-internal decisions. A client verb named 'admit' that the client can invoke is not admission control — it is a suggestion box. The owner admits or reconciles on its own authority; clients observe the outcome via status.

caller_binding.mechanism: Setup-issued caller handles. At owner startup, trusted setup registers exactly two handles (medic, rivet) with the owner process directly — never via a client verb. Each request carries its handle.
caller_binding.revocation: Owner-side only: setup instructs the owner to drop a handle. A dropped handle's requests are refused; its leases enter the uncertainty-hold path, not silent release.
caller_binding.honest_limits: This is NOT OS process isolation. A handle is a bearer token presented over the transport. Against a local attacker with the same privileges it is forgeable. What it does provide: (1) the owner never accepts an unregistered handle, (2) revocation is immediate and owner-enforced, (3) handles are never client-mintable. I claim no more than the existing routes support.

transport_boundary.windows_reality: No Unix sockets on the target host (Windows laptop). The viable loopback transports are a named pipe or loopback TCP — both require a listener, which is future activation work, not this design.
transport_boundary.this_design_defines: The protocol (verbs, handle binding, lease semantics) independent of transport. Transport selection and qualification belong to the later activation gate.

caller_paths_assumed.medic: SSH to laptop -> local client stub that speaks the owner protocol over the future loopback transport. Medic never exposes the owner beyond loopback.
caller_paths_assumed.rivet: UNRESOLVED — see local question. If your relay reaches the laptop, your path mirrors mine. If not, your path terminates at a client stub on your own host and the transport gap is real, not just unbuilt.

preserved_invariants: Exclusive operator ownership: one lease holder per route at a time, enforced by the single _owners dict.
Expiry: leases carry deadlines; expiry moves the lease to uncertainty-hold, not auto-release.
Durable uncertainty: after expiry, revocation, or owner restart, the route stays in uncertain state until independent quiescence evidence arrives.
Quiescence before transfer: no lease transfers without evidence the previous holder is quiescent.

fake_backend_tests.harness: In-process fake transport: two client stubs + owner in one test process, transport replaced by direct calls. No sockets, no processes.
cases: shared_owner_identity: both stubs see the same lease state; a lease granted via stub A is visible and exclusive via stub B.
unauthorized_operations: stub with unregistered handle gets refusal on every verb; stub A cannot release stub B's lease.
stale_revoked_callers: after owner drops stub B's handle, B's requests refuse and B's leases enter uncertainty-hold.
competing_requests: concurrent request_lease from both stubs yields exactly one holder; the loser gets a deterministic refusal, not a silent queue.
lost_replies: client that never receives the grant response must re-query status rather than assume; owner state is the single truth.
restart_holds: owner restart empties state; pre-restart leases are not honored; routes enter uncertain state.
bounded_cleanup: owner stop releases all leases to uncertain state and refuses new requests; no dangling holders.

payload.local_question_for_rivet: Through your recovered native-local relay, run `hostname` (and, if permitted, resolve the laptop's Tailscale address). Expected evidence: either the hostname matches the laptop (your caller path can reach the owner host directly) or it does not (your path needs a remote stub, and the transport gap is architectural, not just unbuilt). No listener, no UI action, read-only.
unresolved_assumptions: Rivet's caller path to the laptop (answered by the local question above).
Whether loopback named pipe or loopback TCP is the better Windows transport — deferred to the activation gate, not decided here.
Supervision of the owner process lifetime — out of scope for this design; the design only requires that SOME trusted setup owns start/stop.
payload.scope_restated: Source-only protocol design. No listener, no supervision, no credentials, no transport activation, no live input. The fake-backend tests validate the protocol; transport qualification is a separate future gate.
